A hospital shift-handoff app where outgoing nurses write patient notes and incoming nurses read them, but front-desk staff must never see clinical notes, only appointment schedules.

A landlord-tenant maintenance portal where tenants file repair requests and landlords assign contractors, but contractors can only see requests assigned to them, never the full building's request history.
A university grading system where professors enter grades and students view their own, but a student must never be able to see another student's grade for any assignment.

A corporate expense report tool where employees submit receipts and managers approve them, but an employee must never be able to approve their own expense report even if they also have a manager role.
A daycare app where staff log incidents and only the center director can edit or delete a submitted incident report - staff can add but never modify after submission.
A ride-share driver payout system where drivers see their own earnings and dispatchers see all drivers' earnings, but a driver must never query another driver's payout data through the API.
A software team's on-call rotation tool where engineers see the schedule and only the team lead can override an on-call assignment - the override must be logged with who made the change and why.
A subscription box service where customers manage their own billing and support staff can view but never edit a customer's payment method directly.

A shared vacation-home booking calendar for extended family where any family member can request dates but only the two owners can approve a booking, and a rejected request must not silently become approved later.
A voting app for a homeowners association where residents cast one vote per household and the board can view aggregate results but never see how an individual household voted.
A freelance marketplace where clients post jobs and freelancers bid, but a freelancer must never see a competing freelancer's bid amount before submitting their own.
A internal bug tracker where developers file and close bugs, but only QA can mark a bug as verified-fixed - a developer closing their own bug does not count as verification.
A school field trip payment app where parents pay a fee and the school treasurer reconciles payments, but teachers organizing the trip can see who has paid, never the payment method or card details.
A restaurant loyalty points system where customers redeem points and staff issue them at checkout, but a customer must never be able to issue points to their own account directly.
A construction site safety inspection app where inspectors file reports and site managers respond, but a site manager must never edit an inspector's original findings, only add a response.

A community lending library for board games where members borrow and return games, and only librarians can mark a game as lost or damaged - a member reporting damage does not itself change the game's status.
A telehealth app where patients book video visits with doctors, and billing staff can see appointment times and durations for invoicing but must never access the visit's clinical summary.
A co-working space access system where members badge in with their own credentials, and front-desk staff can see who is currently in the building but never a member's full entry/exit history.
